_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- TELESCOPES mode: ESO Very Large Telescope, Unit Telescopes UT1-UT4 (all foci; entrance pupil)
_meta.companion: data/telescopes/vlt.md (same content as Markdown). Structure as keck.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; common (shared UT design: params, machine-readable pupil, primary, combined foci, not_found, conflicts, notes); ut1..ut4 each with telescope{name, site, mount, optical_design, primary, pupil, foci[]}, params, not_found, conflicts, notes. Focus and pupil fields carry refs (common.<param> / utN.<param>) into the sourced params.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/vlt/ (files reused from earlier rounds are byte-identical copies, marked in the cite). derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure (not text-checkable; the caption or link-text quote is checked). INFERRED = a reasoned mapping no source states. NOT FOUND = a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_check: 160 quotes machine-checked against the saved files' extracted text (pdftotext -layout and -raw for PDFs; tag-stripped text and raw source for HTML, decoded as UTF-8 or windows-1252; the .py as is): all pass (2026-10-19). GIF figures are not text-checkable: their values are FIGURE READ-OFFs attached to a checked caption or link-text quote.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), division slash, tilde operator and soft hyphens normalised; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with PDF line-end hyphenation removed or closed up, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces.
_meta.design_vs_asbuilt: WB (1998) and SPEC (2005) give the nominal design of the UTs; EM1/WB Table 3.3 the as-built primaries; EINS (May 2026) the current instrument locations; A13/A17 the UT4 deformable secondary (2016); HCI the pupil model after the ERIS pupil document.
_meta.pupil_frame: Vane coordinates are in the hcipy make_vlt_aperture frame (metres on the pupil, angle from +x; each vane a segment from start_xy to end_xy). The orientation of this frame relative to the elevation axis and the Nasmyth A/B sides is not documented.
